newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet after fall in Japan market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet after fall in Japan market.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market remained quiet by the midday break on Wednesday with several potential buyers sidelined by falling prices in the Japanese rubber market, dealers said.
"With Japan down quite a lot, everybody was sidelined. I did not see any new orders come in this morning," a dealer said.
The benchmark September contract in Tokyo fell 1.2 yen to 139.6. It had also closed 1.2 yen down on Tuesday.
"There were no bits of orders that came into the market this morning. We'll have to wait for the afternoon to see if something will pick us up," another dealer said.
Thai sellers were also groping for direction after coming back from the long Songkran Buddhist holidays, dealers said.
Dealers said the market will also find it difficult to get leads tomorrow before the Eid Al-Adha Moslem holiday on Friday, which will close markets in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia.
At around 0445 GMT, June RSS3 was indicated at 112.00-113.00 U.S. cents a kg from 114.00 cents.

June RSS1 was indicated at 161.00-163.00 Singapore cents (US$1.11-$1.13) a kg from 163.00 cents. June TSR20 was indicated at 153.50-155.50 Singapore cents a kg (US$1.06-$1.08) from 155.50 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
